facts.assertion: Enfield's emerging Local Plan covers the period 2019 to 2039.
Enfield says it is preparing the new Local Plan to shape future development in the borough.
Enfield's most recent call for sites ran in June and July 2022.
The 2022 call for sites closed on 15 July 2022.
Enfield says land availability will be kept under annual review until the new Local Plan is adopted.
Enfield describes call for sites as an early opportunity to suggest land available for development.
Enfield says call-for-sites submissions inform preparation of the Local Plan.
Enfield explicitly says call for sites does not determine whether a site should be allocated.
Enfield says call-for-sites submissions form a potential pool for technical assessment.
Publication of a submitted site does not indicate it will be allocated.
Publication of a submitted site does not indicate it will obtain planning permission.
Enfield tests sites for suitability, availability and achievability.
Housing and employment sites are considered through the HELAA.
HELAA technical assessment is not equivalent to adopted site allocation.
Enfield states the plan and associated sites undergo independent examination before adoption.
Full Council approved the emerging Enfield Local Plan for Regulation 19 publication on 19 March 2024.
The Regulation 19 consultation ran from 28 March to 20 May 2024.
Enfield submitted the Local Plan to the Secretary of State for examination on 6 August 2024.
The current Enfield Local Plan page presents the process as Regulation 24 Examination in Public.
The Regulation 19 document list includes Appendix C Site Allocations.
The Regulation 19 document list includes policies-map material.
Appendix C Site Allocations is plan-stage evidence and not candidate row 30762 point-in-polygon membership by itself.
Enfield's examination library includes proposed modifications.
Enfield's examination library includes updated housing trajectory evidence.
The Planning Inspector issued a post-hearing letter to Enfield Council on 15 June 2026.
Enfield says the Inspector's June 2026 letter identifies further Main Modifications or steps needed for soundness and legal compliance.
Enfield reports the Inspector recommended removing certain development sites from the Green Belt.
The Inspector's recommendation does not identify candidate row 30762 without exact site-reference or geometry binding.
The Enfield Local Plan page records a Council response to the Inspector's post-hearing letter dated 29 June 2026.
The new Local Plan remains examination-stage evidence rather than an adopted replacement plan at this checkpoint.
Candidate row 30762 remains unbound to a borough-confirmed positive allocation polygon.
The published GLA Site Allocations layer-102 full envelope excludes row 30762 on the northing axis.
GLA describes Site Allocations boundaries as indicative and directs users to boroughs to confirm boundary accuracy.
Therefore the GLA layer-102 extent exclusion is not promoted to a borough-confirmed negative allocation decision for row 30762.
The Enfield GLA local-plan FeatureServer exposes multiple growth-related layers, but layer taxonomy alone is not membership.
No exact candidate point-query response for Enfield allocation/growth layers was produced in this continuation.
Unexecuted parameterized queries are not converted into positive membership.
Unexecuted parameterized queries are not converted into negative membership.
Production 330-job hashed execution remains incomplete and separate from this plan-stage audit.
No business score is promoted for row 30762 from Call for Sites, HELAA, Regulation 19, examination correspondence or GLA indicative extent exclusion.
